title: Perfekt: Sentence Structure
sourceNote: Transcript is mostly clean. The exercise sentences were shown on screen; only the teacher's spoken answers are in the transcript.
objectives: I can explain what the Perfekt is and when it is used
I can build a Perfekt statement: Hilfsverb in position 2, Partizip II at the end
I can form W-questions and yes/no questions in the Perfekt
I can use separable verbs and modal verbs in past sentences

expressions.de: Am Freitag sind wir ins Kino gegangen.
expressions.en: On Friday we went to the cinema.

grammar.title: What is the Perfekt?
grammar.body:
German has three past forms: **Plusquamperfekt** (later level), **Präteritum** (A2; you already know it for *sein* and *haben*: *war*, *hatte*) and **Perfekt**. The **Perfekt** is the past tense used most in **spoken German** and in private or half-formal letters.

Three things to learn: (1) the sentence structure, (2) when to use *haben* and when *sein* (next lesson), (3) how to form the **Partizip II** (later lesson).
grammar.ar: الـ Perfekt هو الماضي الأكثر استخدامًا في الكلام اليومي.

grammar.title: Structure of the Perfekt
grammar.body:
In the present tense the verb is in position 2. In the Perfekt the **Hilfsverb** (**haben** or **sein**, conjugated) is in **position 2** and the main verb moves to the **end** as **Partizip II**.

Always learn the Partizip II together with its helping verb: *essen – hat gegessen*, *fahren – ist gefahren*.

head: Present
Perfekt
rows: Wir sind letzte Woche nach Paris gefahren.
Er hat mit seinem Hund gespielt.

grammar.ar: الفعل المساعد في المرتبة الثانية، واسم المفعول (Partizip II) في آخر الجملة.

grammar.title: Questions in the Perfekt
grammar.body: **W-question:** question word first, Hilfsverb in position 2, Partizip II at the end. **Yes/no question:** Hilfsverb in position **1**, Partizip II at the end.

grammar.title: Separable verbs
grammar.body: With a separable verb the Partizip II also goes to the end, but it is formed differently (more in lesson 46). Here: *anrufen – hat angerufen*.

grammar.title: Modal verbs in the past
grammar.body: With a modal verb, German normally uses the **Präteritum** of the modal (you learn it in A2) and an **infinitive** at the end, not the Perfekt. Just recognise it for now.

examples.de: Ich bin krank. Ich muss zum Arzt gehen.
examples.en: I am ill. I have to go to the doctor.

examples.de: Ich war krank. Ich musste zum Arzt gehen.
examples.en: I was ill. I had to go to the doctor.

grammar.title: Word order is flexible at the start
grammar.body: A time expression can start the sentence, but the Hilfsverb stays in position 2: *Am Freitag **sind** wir ins Kino gegangen.* = *Wir **sind** am Freitag ins Kino gegangen.*

mistakes.why: Partizip II goes to the very end.
The Hilfsverb must be in position 2.

lines.de: Ich habe nur drei Stunden geschlafen und dann Hausaufgaben gemacht.
lines.en: I only slept three hours and then did homework.

lines.de: Ja, ich habe einen Salat gegessen.

tip: Memorise each verb as a chunk with its helper: hat gegessen, ist gefahren, hat gespielt, hat studiert, hat gemacht, hat angerufen.

comprehension.q: Which helping verbs can the Perfekt use?
Where is the Hilfsverb in a Perfekt statement?

comprehension.a: At the end of the sentence.

exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

exercises.instructions: Choose the correct Hilfsverb. Use the verb list from this lesson.

summary: The Perfekt is the main spoken past tense.
Structure: Hilfsverb (haben/sein) in position 2 + Partizip II at the end.
Yes/no questions start with the Hilfsverb; W-questions start with the W-word, then the Hilfsverb.
Learn each Partizip II with its helper: hat gegessen, ist gefahren.
With modal verbs, German uses the Präteritum (later lesson).
